analysis.summary: PD-20-1440 is technically adjacent to METSS Corporation’s applied chemistry, functional-fluid, microbiology/CBRN, formulation, analytical, and testing capabilities, but it is not a direct match to the public record of METSS past performance. The central program requirement is potentially transformative fundamental environmental-engineering research with a clear connection to pollution prevention, remediation, environmental treatment efficiency, or pollutant transport and biogeochemical reactivity. METSS should not pursue a generic materials, sensing, testing-service, decontamination, or manufacturing-scale-up concept under this program. A credible path exists only if METSS can form an environmental-engineering-led research team and develop a mechanism-focused project where METSS has a substantive chemistry, treatment-formulation, analytical-validation, or transition work package. Regular proposals have no stated deadline, but the current availability and topic fit should be confirmed with the Program Director before proposal investment.
analysis.immediate_action: Conduct a short internal qualification review to identify a specific environmental problem and METSS work package tied to treatment mechanisms or pollutant biogeochemical reactivity; simultaneously verify SAM/UEI/AOR and proposed-PI readiness. If a concept and environmental-engineering academic lead are identified, contact the Environmental Engineering Program Director with a concise concept summary before committing to a full proposal. Do not proceed if the concept is principally materials development, monitoring, routine testing, or product scale-up without the required fundamental environmental-engineering research question.

deepAccepted.title: Advanced Manufacturing
deepAccepted.summary: PD-19-088Y is technically relevant to METSS’s broad applied-research identity, particularly advanced materials, specialty chemistry, process development, pilot-scale scale-up, and testing/validation. METSS has credible public evidence for a meaningful technical work package such as materials/process development, manufacturability studies, formulation and processing optimization, and performance/compatibility validation. However, this is framed as an NSF fundamental-research program, and neither current opportunity activity nor METSS’s administrative eligibility and proposal readiness is proven. Investigate rather than pursue now; a prime-versus-partner decision should follow confirmation of current status, NSF eligibility mechanics, and availability of a compelling fundamental research concept.
deepAccepted.why: The opportunity seeks fundamental, multidisciplinary advanced-manufacturing research, including materials processing, materials engineering and processing, manufacturing systems, equipment, methodologies, and cross-scale manufacturing.: The reviewed program description identifies these areas as examples and encourages interdisciplinary proposals that transform manufacturing capabilities, methods, and practices. (NSF Program Desccription PD-19-088Y) METSS has an evidence-backed technical basis for manufacturing-focused materials and chemistry work.: METSS publicly identifies organic materials, polymers, composites, coatings, adhesives, specialty resins, functional fluids, formulation/product development, mechanical and chemical engineering, and product/process design from laboratory development through commercial production. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS can contribute validation and transition-oriented work packages relevant to manufacturing-process and materials-development projects.: The profile identifies chemical, physical, mechanical, environmental, performance, and materials-compatibility testing, together with pilot-scale operations and light manufacturing. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS has publicly documented prior work relevant to materials development, manufacturing scale-up, and industrial supply resilience.: Public examples include Advanced Lightweight Composite Structures for Ground Vehicle Systems; Non-PFAS Elastomeric Chemical Barrier Materials; Critical Supply Chain Production of Energetic Materials and Associated Precursors; and DPA Title III Critical Chemicals Production. (Approved METSS public profile)
deepAccepted.action: Before allocating capture or proposal resources, retrieve and verify the current official NSF status page and current PAPPG applicability; confirm METSS SAM/UEI/NSF submission readiness; then send a concise concept outline to AdvancedManufacturing@nsf.gov for program-director feedback. Advance only if METSS can define a fundamental advanced-manufacturing research question with clear intellectual merit, broader impacts, and a credible technical/transition work package.

METSS has a plausible supporting work package where advanced materials, EMI/harsh-environment performance, chemical/biological survivability, or controlled testing can generate credible data for an EMP-shielding, personnel-survivability, vulnerability, reliability, sustainment, or DAC-competency concept. analysis.summary: This is a strategically strong technical match for METSS’s applied-research identity in CBRN protection/decontamination, advanced polymers and barrier materials, specialty chemistry, and validation under harsh conditions. The strongest historical topic alignments were Amendment 2 B4 (PFAS-free omniphobic protective materials) and B6 (cross-linked polymer detection films), supported by both official topic scope and METSS public materials, chemistry, testing, and CBRN evidence. However, B1–B6 closed on March 2, 2026, and the supplied record does not establish an extension. METSS therefore should not treat the expired topics as available. A general-thrust Phase I submission may remain possible under the continuing BAA through September 30, 2034, but only after DTRA technical pre-coordination and confirmation of a viable funding path. METSS has an evidence-backed potential prime role for a materials/protection/decontamination-focused fundamental-research concept, but prime eligibility remains conditional on administrative and proposal-specific requirements.

analysis.summary: This is a strategically relevant broad DARPA BAA with plausible METSS work-package fit in advanced materials, specialty chemistry/functional fluids, test and validation, and manufacturing scale-up. METSS's public profile supports an initial investigation because TTO explicitly values manufacturability, production responsiveness, supply-chain alternatives, and accelerated testing. However, the BAA is not a generic materials or domestic-manufacturing solicitation: it requires a revolutionary, quantitatively defensible concept tied to DARPA military mission impact. No such METSS-specific concept, team, readiness confirmation, or DARPA engagement is supplied. Accordingly, technical relevance is meaningful but not yet sufficient for a pursue recommendation or a defined prime/subcontract role. The operative supplied schedule is an Executive Summary due April 17, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. ET and a full proposal due June 22, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. ET; a full proposal additionally requires DARPA's signed Encourage Full Proposal letter.
analysis.immediate_action: Before April 17, 2026 at 4:00 p.m. ET, conduct a rapid internal concept gate: identify one METSS-owned, non-generic revolutionary concept with a measurable TTO outcome in Design/Build/Buy or Surge and Sustain; confirm whether METSS already has an Executive Summary under DARPA review; verify SAM/responsibility, OCI, resource, pricing, and classification posture; and determine whether METSS will lead or needs a systems/transition partner. If these checks support a credible concept, submit a compliant two-page Executive Summary through DARPA BAAT—not Grants.gov—and use DARPA feedback to determine whether to prepare a full proposal. Do not commit to classified tasks or an OT cost-share position without separate verification.
caveats: The supplied SAM.gov material was not independently readable as a current opportunity-status record; timing is based on the supplied BAA and amendment findings.

analysis.summary: This is a commercialization bridge program, not an open technical-topic solicitation. It is technically adjacent to METSS where an eligible NIH Phase II/IIB small-business awardee needs late-stage formulation/materials work, analytical or performance validation, process optimization, manufacturing scale-up, or specialized technical assistance. METSS has evidence for those potential subcontract functions. However, the public profile does not establish the mandatory NIH Phase II/IIB award or SBC eligibility required for METSS to prime, and it identifies no specific NIH-aligned product or commercialization project. Investigate only as a targeted subcontracting opportunity or after internal confirmation of a qualifying METSS NIH Phase II/IIB award. The earliest stated deadline is September 5, 2026 at 5:00 PM local time; a broad availability window does not establish that a suitable NIH component or project is available.
analysis.immediate_action: Conduct an internal gate before expending capture resources: confirm whether METSS itself has an eligible NIH SBIR/STTR Phase II/IIB award and current SBC/registration status. If not, identify an eligible U.S. CRP prime with a compatible NIH-supported technology and obtain a written request for a narrowly defined METSS domestic subcontract work package; verify NIH Institute/Center mission fit with the relevant program staff before bid development.

analysis.summary: Do not pursue as METSS Corporation. The opportunity is technically adjacent to METSS formulation, materials, and testing capabilities, but it is narrowly intended for applicants that already possess a mature, characterized contraceptive or reproductive-health product program and need NICHD BTF services. The approved METSS profile provides no evidence of such a program, validated target/mechanism, test article, reproductive preclinical package, or meaningful funded work package for METSS. Although for-profit entities are eligible in principle, required registrations and account status are unknown. The next listed application deadline is September 7, 2026, at 5:00 PM applicant-organization local time; later cycles run through May 7, 2029. The strongest current path is to investigate a university-led collaboration or a METSS-led submission only after eligibility and research-lead requirements are verified. This is not yet an evidence-backed pursue decision.

(Approved METSS public profile) METSS materials and polymer capabilities align with CPS interest in process and materials innovation, including polymer processing and scalable chemical-process technologies.: METSS publicly lists polymers, composite resins, coatings, adhesives, specialty resins, packaging and barrier films, polymer processing and recycling, and materials for harsh chemical environments. deepAccepted.title: Measurement Science and Engineering (MSE) Research Grant Programs
deepAccepted.agency: National Institute of Standards and Technology
deepAccepted.summary: This is a technically relevant broad NIST research vehicle, with the strongest apparent METSS path in MML-aligned materials, chemical, biological, or biomolecular measurement research. METSS’s public advanced-materials, specialty-chemistry, analytical, validation, and CBRN-testing capabilities support a meaningful potential work package, and its public past performance reinforces applied research credibility. Nevertheless, the opportunity is not yet a clear pursue decision because the NOFO requires alignment to a specific component and current division-level objective, while the supplied materials do not confirm an active METSS-relevant topic or funding capacity. METSS is eligible in principle as a for-profit non-Federal entity, but formal submission eligibility and operational readiness remain conditional on unverified registrations and proposal-specific requirements. The appropriate role is conditional prime applicant for a narrowly scoped research project, not a commercialization or product-development proposal.
deepAccepted.why: The opportunity includes a plausible measurement-science research path through the Materials Measurement Laboratory (MML), including materials, chemical, biological, and biomolecular measurement topics.: The reviewed NOFO identifies MML among the 13 MSE component programs and describes materials, chemical, biological, and biomolecular measurement within the program scope. (FY25 MSE NOFO Amendment.pdf) METSS has public capabilities relevant to experimental materials and chemical measurement research, including formulation, characterization, analytical work, compatibility testing, and performance evaluation.: METSS publicly lists advanced-materials development; physical, organic, inorganic, and analytical chemistry; sample analysis; reaction characterization; formulation and product development; and chemical, physical, mechanical, environmental, performance, and materials-compatibility testing. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS has relevant applied-R&D past-performance examples in materials, chemical barriers, functional fluids, and CBRN survivability.: Public examples include Non-PFAS Elastomeric Chemical Barrier Materials; Lubricating Oil Study; Vapor Purge and Chemical Agent Persistence in Aircraft; Aircraft and Sensitive Equipment CBRN Survivability Capability Development and Transition; and Compact Sensor for Non-Destructive Propellant Mechanical Property Evaluation. (Approved METSS public profile) METSS can be an eligible applicant type in principle because the NOFO is open to for-profit organizations.: The record states that the NOFO is open to all non-Federal entities, expressly including for-profit organizations. (Official Grants.gov record)
deepAccepted.action: Before committing bid resources, identify a candidate MML measurement-science concept and contact the current applicable NIST program office to confirm objective fit, active funding/topic availability, expected award structure, and any component-specific limits. analysis.summary: This is not a direct METSS grant opportunity. Its core requirement is five years of continuous, jurisdiction-authorized BioWatch field operations, with laboratory operations in certain locations; R&D projects are expressly unallowable. METSS has relevant public bioaerosol, BSL-2, analytical-testing, decontamination, and CBRN experience that could support a narrowly defined subcontract work package, but the profile does not prove the operational scale, 24/7/365 readiness, jurisdictional authority, staffing, security, or laboratory-reporting capability required for award performance. analysis.summary: This record does not support pursuit. While METSS's documented polymer/materials and testing capabilities create limited conceptual relevance to the word “microplastics,” the official record contains no scope or technical requirements that establish a meaningful, evidence-backed METSS work package. The public profile also does not establish microplastics-specific or U24 research-center coordination past performance. Eligibility is unknown, not affirmative. Under the screening rules, the absence of a defined technical role and reliance on broad keyword-level overlap require a do-not-pursue determination.
analysis.immediate_action: Do not allocate capture or proposal resources. If METSS later requests reconsideration, first obtain the official NIH funding announcement and all amendments through Grants.gov/NIH, then reassess eligibility, due dates, center functions, required partnerships, and whether a defined METSS materials or analytical-testing work package exists.

analysis.summary: This is a strategically relevant but premature opportunity. METSS's public chemistry, functional-fluids, analytical/testing, process-development, pilot-scale, and domestic-supply-chain capabilities could support a meaningful work package in chemical formulation, process optimization, materials compatibility, analytical validation, scale-up support, or product qualification. The available record does not establish that METSS possesses a qualifying alternative/waste-feedstock conversion technology or the integrated pre-pilot facility readiness likely needed for a lead Topic Area 2 effort. Because this is only an NOI, no application is currently permitted, and binding eligibility and cost-share terms remain unknown. METSS should investigate and form a capability-specific team rather than commit to priming at this stage.
analysis.immediate_action: Before the anticipated August 24, 2026 NOFO release, identify one METSS-owned, evidence-supported candidate work package and determine whether an external technology owner has a defined alternative/waste-feedstock-to-chemical pathway. In parallel, obtain human verification of METSS's SAM.gov/UEI and legal entity status, assess cost-share and available pilot/testing capacity, register or confirm access to DOE eXCHANGE as appropriate, and monitor the official DOE/Grants.gov release for binding requirements.
caveats: This assessment is based on the Grants.gov NOI and the supplied attachment only; the anticipated NOFO is not an active solicitation and may materially change or never be issued.
